entry_criteria.description: Name the product/maintenance owner and the release or CI owner.
Identify a user problem that is not already served by an existing Surface.
Reuse the shared Go Application contract, or provide a bounded adapter decision and threat model; never introduce renderer-owned authority or a second state machine.
Review Scope, policy, approval, credential, network, process, persistence, privacy, and recovery impact.
Declare the supported OS/runtime matrix together with accessibility and bilingual-copy obligations.
Name normal, refusal, timeout, cancel, restart, upgrade, downgrade, cleanup, and release-blocking evidence proportional to the authority exposed.
Declare public and durable compatibility obligations, support signals, and an export path without assuming usage telemetry.
Declare the notice date/window and tagged prereleases required before downgrade or removal.
Provide removal, recovery, and rollback plans that preserve published protocol and durable identity obligations.
Keep the implementation independently removable and prevent optional extensions from becoming startup dependencies.

governance.authority_statement: This registry describes product support levels only. It grants no file, process, network, browser, Docker, credential, approval, Scope, or runtime capability.
governance.rollback_statement: The registry/check may be reverted, but a revert cannot silently change a published protocol, durable identity, compatibility promise, or user-data recovery obligation.

owners.name: Desktop/Product maintainers
responsibilities: Desktop and React product entry points

tiers.product_commitment: Core product work and release evidence through the shared Go Application contract.
Existing users and automation remain supported; no new workflow is admitted at this tier.
The seam and its Go-owned safety boundary are supported; optional implementations are not core release requirements.
No current implementation or release promise.

entries.name: Windows and macOS Wails Desktop
entries.application_contract: The Wails shell uses the in-process authenticated Go HTTP handler and the same internal/application services as CLI and loopback Web.
entries.authority_impact: The renderer is presentation-only; Go retains Scope, policy, approval, credential, process, persistence, and recovery authority.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep Windows/macOS packaged startup, shared store access, and historical executable/data identities compatible; do not create a Desktop-only authority path.
entries.deprecation_window: Downgrade requires a separate decision and supported replacement; removal follows at least 90 days and two tagged prereleases at maintenance-only.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore the packaged shell against the same Go handler and retained identities; never roll back by deleting user data or published protocol readers.
entries.boundary: Primary packaged product; build, startup, renderer-integrity, and recovery checks are release-blocking.

entries.name: React/Vite Thread workbench
entries.application_contract: One renderer consumes authenticated Go HTTP/bridge projections backed by internal/application; TypeScript cannot mint durable identity or authority.
entries.authority_impact: UI state is non-authorizing presentation; all mutations, permissions, approvals, and recovery decisions are validated in Go. Project preparation submits explicit lock-bound package source and install-script selections to Go; web search retains its independent setting.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep the React renderer shared by Desktop and authenticated loopback Web, preserve API v1 projections, and converge primary navigation on Thread without renaming durable IDs.
entries.deprecation_window: Downgrade requires a supported user workflow replacement; removal follows at least 90 days and two tagged prereleases at maintenance-only.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore the same renderer bundle and Go projections; preserve exported receipts, API compatibility, and user-data recovery.
entries.boundary: Shared renderer for Desktop and authenticated loopback Web; Thread is primary and TypeScript remains presentation-only.

entries.name: cyberagent CLI
entries.application_contract: cmd/cyberagent delegates command handling to internal/app and the shared internal/application services and stores.
entries.authority_impact: CLI flags select requests only; Go-owned validation retains Scope, policy, approval, credential, process, persistence, and recovery authority.
entries.compatibility_strategy: The cyberagent executable name and established flags/output contracts remain compatibility identifiers while Thread/Run/Workspace presentation converges.
entries.deprecation_window: A successor must preserve automation and recovery before downgrade; removal follows at least 90 days and two tagged prereleases at maintenance-only.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore command adapters over the same Application services and durable identities; retain old-client fixtures and machine-readable output compatibility.
entries.boundary: Stable operator and automation entry; the executable name is a compatibility ID, not a second control plane.

entries.name: Loopback HTTP and OpenAPI /api/v1
entries.application_contract: internal/httpapi is an authenticated adapter over the shared internal/application contract used by Web and Desktop clients.
entries.authority_impact: Literal loopback binding and bearer separation gate access; handlers cannot widen Go-owned Scope, policy, approval, credential, or persistence decisions.
release_blocking_checks: CI / TypeScript console API drift check
entries.compatibility_strategy: Preserve /api/v1 routes, DTOs, generated OpenAPI, loopback-only binding, and process-local token separation; it is not a hosted service.
entries.deprecation_window: External route retirement follows protocol governance in addition to at least 90 days and two tagged prereleases after any Surface downgrade.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore handlers over the same Application contract and retain old-client/OpenAPI fixtures; a Surface transition cannot delete published routes or durable readers.
entries.boundary: Authenticated literal-loopback API used by first-party clients and integrations; never a multi-tenant remote control plane. Conversation web access follows the shared Go Run snapshot contract (ADR 0175), independently of command and sandbox scope. Project preparation (ADR 0176) binds package downloads to the inspected lockfile and exact operator-selected HTTPS origins, then installs offline in the selected sandbox through the existing Command Runtime.

entries.name: Bubble Tea TUI
entries.application_contract: internal/tui consumes bounded projections and internal/app controls over the same Go stores and Application services.
entries.authority_impact: TUI selections do not mint identity or bypass Go policy, approval, Scope, credential, or persistence validation.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Accept only security, compatibility, data-loss, and severe-defect fixes; new primary workflows target Thread workbench and CLI after an explicit promotion.
entries.deprecation_window: Removal requires at least 90 days and two tagged prereleases after notice, plus a supported replacement.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Retain terminal compatibility and recovery fixtures; restore the adapter without changing Go stores, authority, or durable identities.
entries.boundary: Read/control compatibility and critical fixes remain supported; feature parity is not a beta release gate.

entries.name: headless event/CI commands
entries.application_contract: internal/app headless commands use the same Go Application lifecycle and event projections as interactive entry points.
entries.authority_impact: Automation input remains subject to Go-owned Scope, policy, approval, execution, and persistence checks.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep deterministic events and existing scripts compatible; accept only security, compatibility, data-loss, and severe-defect fixes without promotion.
entries.deprecation_window: Removal requires at least 90 days and two tagged prereleases after notice, with replacement automation and old-client fixtures.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore the headless adapter and event projection over unchanged Application services and durable identities.
entries.boundary: Existing deterministic CI and event automation remains supported; it is not another interactive product or authority path.

entries.name: /runs/{id} and /sessions/{id} diagnostic views/routes
entries.application_contract: Legacy diagnostics are read/control projections over the shared Go Application and HTTP API contracts.
entries.authority_impact: Run/Session routes remain diagnostics and compatibility identities; they cannot become alternate task authority or bypass Thread/Run validation.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Retain API and diagnostic compatibility; accept only security, compatibility, data-loss, and severe-defect fixes, not new primary workflows.
entries.deprecation_window: Published routes also follow protocol retirement rules; Surface removal still requires at least 90 days and two tagged prereleases.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Keep old-client and old-store fixtures and restore projections without renaming or deleting Run/Session durable identities.
entries.boundary: Diagnostics and API compatibility only; these routes are not alternate stable task identities.

entries.name: MCP client and Go-controlled MCP server
entries.application_contract: internal/mcp negotiation and invocation enter only through reviewed Go tool/application adapters.
entries.authority_impact: Discovery is non-authorizing; Go retains policy, independent approval, Scope, timeout, audit, and credential boundaries.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep protocol negotiation, parser, audit, timeout, and cancellation contracts compatible; core use and release never require an MCP server.
entries.deprecation_window: Contract retirement requires a separate decision, compatibility evidence, notice, and the registry default removal window unless a security advisory shortens it.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Disable or restore the optional adapter without changing core startup, Go authority, durable identities, or non-MCP workflows.
entries.boundary: Optional discovery and invocation seam behind Go review and policy; never a core startup dependency.

entries.name: Signed Plugin and restricted Hook runtime
entries.application_contract: internal/plugins produces inert reviewed content for Go-owned application and tool adapters; hooks remain explicitly restricted.
entries.authority_impact: Plugin/Hook bytes grant no process, network, credential, file, approval, or Scope authority; Go validates every later use.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Support signed package/parser compatibility and security fixes while keeping imported content inert and optional.
entries.deprecation_window: Contract removal requires a separate supply-chain decision and the registry default notice window unless a security advisory applies.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Disable the optional import/runtime seam while retaining readable package metadata and a recoverable uninstall/restore path.
entries.boundary: Signed or reviewed content remains inert by default and cannot self-authorize host capabilities.

entries.name: Skill packages and registries
entries.application_contract: internal/skills contributes bounded manifests and content to Go-owned selection, policy, and application flows.
entries.authority_impact: Third-party packages are untrusted and optional; provenance and manifest fields cannot grant tool, process, network, credential, approval, or Scope authority.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Built-in Skills may support core workflows, but third-party packages remain optional with signed/pinned provenance where required.
entries.deprecation_window: Package-format retirement requires reader compatibility, export/uninstall recovery, and the registry default notice window unless a security advisory applies.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore the prior reader/registry while preserving inert package bytes and selections; never make third-party availability a startup dependency.
entries.boundary: Third-party packages are untrusted optional extensions; package metadata never confers runtime authority.

entries.name: Rust/WASI and local analyzer contracts
entries.application_contract: Analyzer candidates and results cross versioned contracts into Go-owned application admission, Scope/approval, staging, and recovery controls.
entries.authority_impact: Go is the sole control plane; analyzers cannot own Agent, Session, secret, host-process lifecycle, approval, or Scope.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep analyzer formats, golden vectors, isolation checks, and recovery contracts supported without requiring an analyzer for core startup or release.
entries.deprecation_window: Format retirement follows protocol governance and the registry default notice window unless an emergency advisory applies.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Disable the optional adapter and restore prior contract readers/golden vectors without widening Go authority or losing staged-result recovery.
entries.boundary: Supported optional contracts and backend seam; analyzers cannot become a second control plane.

entries.name: Windows AppContainer and fixed Docker Standard Code
entries.application_contract: Backends are selected and driven only by Go-owned Application readiness, permission, Drydock, command-runtime, and supervisor contracts.
entries.authority_impact: Backend availability never grants execution; Scope, permission, approval, ownership, network containment, cleanup, and recovery remain Go-owned.
release_blocking_checks: CI / Windows Desktop shell local-sandbox gate
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep active backend readiness, ownership, network-none/WFP, restart, and exact-cleanup evidence without marketing a new user Surface.
entries.deprecation_window: An active backend downgrade requires a supported execution replacement; removal follows the registry default maintenance window and protocol obligations.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore the backend adapter behind the same Go gates; retain Drydock/checkpoint recovery and never delete user workspaces or durable receipts.
entries.boundary: Active execution backends reached through existing Surfaces; they are not independent user entry points.

entries.name: Browser/CDP runtime and real UI evidence
entries.application_contract: Go Application permission/readiness controls issue bounded browser plans and consume evidence through internal/browserruntime and HTTP/tool adapters.
entries.authority_impact: Browser launch, network, CDP, profile, and evidence access require independent Go permission and containment gates; renderer state is non-authorizing.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep the bounded capability active behind Go gates; do not infer a standalone browser product, arbitrary remote browsing, or renderer-owned CDP.
entries.deprecation_window: Capability downgrade requires replacement evidence for active workflows; removal follows the registry default maintenance window.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore the bounded adapter while retaining profile cleanup/recovery evidence and unchanged Go permission ceilings.
entries.boundary: Bounded active capability and backend; it is not a separate browser product or control plane.

entries.name: Workspace/Git/GitHub Review
entries.application_contract: Workspace, Git mutation, advanced Git, and GitHub Review flows are Go Application capabilities reached through existing CLI/HTTP/Desktop Surfaces.
entries.authority_impact: Workspace Scope, CAS/lease, credential, approval, network-write, and recovery checks remain Go-owned; GitHub availability is optional.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep active local Code workflows and optional credential-scoped GitHub integration without treating the integration as another product Surface.
entries.deprecation_window: Capability downgrade requires a supported local workflow replacement; external contract retirement remains separately governed.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore adapters over the same Workspace/Git identity and recovery model; preserve worktrees, commits, receipts, and credential boundaries.
entries.boundary: Active capabilities and optional integration reached through existing Surfaces; GitHub network writes remain scoped and approval-gated.

entries.name: Checkpoints, batch delivery, and multi-agent coordination
entries.application_contract: Run/Workspace Application services own checkpoints, child-agent scheduling, Drydock/worktree identity, mailbox delivery, merge review, and recovery.
entries.authority_impact: Child agents and worktrees inherit bounded Go-owned Scope, policy, approval, lease, and recovery; coordination cannot create a parallel control plane.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep active Run/Workspace coordination and recovery semantics while exposing them only through existing product Surfaces.
entries.deprecation_window: Capability downgrade requires continuity and recovery replacements; removal follows the registry default maintenance window and durable protocol rules.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Restore coordination adapters without deleting worktrees, checkpoints, mailbox records, receipts, or Run/Workspace identities.
entries.boundary: Active Run/Workspace capabilities; agents, worktrees, and mailboxes do not constitute another product or control plane.

entries.name: ctf command, cyber labels, and offensive workflow skeletons
entries.application_contract: Existing identifiers route only to bounded Go-owned application controls; any real offensive pack requires separate extension admission.
entries.authority_impact: Names grant no target, network, credential, process, approval, or Scope authority.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Keep historical identifiers readable; CTF solving and offensive automation are not core features and need an independently removable approved extension.
entries.deprecation_window: Identifier retirement follows compatibility governance and the registry default notice window unless a security advisory applies.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Disable an optional extension while retaining safe parsing and historical identifiers; restore it only behind the same Go gates.
entries.boundary: Compatibility names and skeletons only; no core offensive product or ambient authority is promised.

entries.name: Cloud/multi-tenant daemon, account sync, hosted control plane
entries.application_contract: No hosted contract exists; entry review must define a bounded adapter over shared Go Application policy without rebranding loopback HTTP.
entries.authority_impact: No authentication, tenancy, remote network, data residency, operations, credential, approval, or support authority is approved.
recovery_evidence: Entry review must define tenant refusal, cancel, restart, export, incident recovery, and cleanup evidence before implementation.
entries.compatibility_strategy: No release promise exists; any future design must keep loopback API v1 compatibility and local-first data/export obligations explicit.
entries.deprecation_window: No implementation may begin until entry review declares a deprecation and removal window.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Reject or withdraw the proposal without mutating runtime; any later implementation must be independently removable and preserve local user data.
entries.boundary: No hosted or multi-tenant product commitment; authenticated loopback HTTP remains local-only.

entries.name: Native Linux Desktop, mobile clients, editor-native full clients
entries.application_contract: No first-party client contract is approved; entry review must bind any client to shared Go Application/API authority rather than duplicate state machines.
entries.authority_impact: No native client may mint identity, persist authority, or bypass Go Scope, policy, approval, credential, network, and recovery controls.
recovery_evidence: Entry review must define offline/refusal, cancel, restart, upgrade, downgrade, export, and cleanup evidence before implementation.
entries.compatibility_strategy: Thin third-party integrations may use the external API; a first-party full client has no release promise until entry review.
entries.deprecation_window: No implementation may begin until entry review declares a deprecation and removal window.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Reject or withdraw the proposal without runtime change; a later client must be independently removable without changing server-side durable identities.
entries.boundary: No native Linux, mobile, or editor full-client release promise; first-party implementation requires entry review.

entries.name: Public extension marketplace and autonomous offensive packs
entries.application_contract: No distribution contract is approved; entry review must retain Go-owned package admission, policy, approval, Scope, provenance, and removal controls.
entries.authority_impact: No marketplace, autonomous target, network, credential, process, moderation, legal, or supply-chain authority is approved.
recovery_evidence: Entry review must define revocation, quarantine, uninstall, export, incident response, and exact cleanup evidence before implementation.
entries.compatibility_strategy: No public distribution promise exists; signed/pinned local extension compatibility remains separate from any future marketplace.
entries.deprecation_window: No implementation may begin until entry review declares moderation, revocation, deprecation, and removal windows.
entries.removal_rollback_plan: Reject or withdraw the proposal without runtime change; any future distribution must be independently disableable with recoverable package state.
entries.boundary: No marketplace or autonomous offensive-pack commitment; supply-chain, moderation, legal, threat, and removal review is mandatory first.
